verdict.summary: A traffic-shaping delay (~300ms) attached to cartservice's network namespace made every Redis call take ~300ms, so cart operations and everything upstream of them slowed and alerted.
verdict.reasoning: Cartservice and checkoutservice logs show normal successful operations with no error text, and the cartservice error-ratio query returned no samples, so this is a latency incident rather than an error incident. Traces show every cartservice Redis hop (HGET/HMSET) taking a near-constant ~300ms of self-time, dominating trace duration and cascading into frontend and checkout latency; the flat, jitter-free magnitude is characteristic of injected network delay rather than organic Redis load. The change history for cartservice shows a repeating experiment pattern including a traffic-shaping container attached to cart-service's network namespace with a 300ms delay, matching the observed per-call penalty exactly.
open_questions: The change records shown end before the 11:48 onset, so the specific delay-injection record for this incident was not directly observed; the recurring pattern is inferred.
Whether the alerts were latency-threshold based or true error-rate alerts was not settled, since the error-ratio series returned no samples.
Redis-side metrics were not examined, so an independent Redis slowdown coincident with the pattern is not fully excluded.
